title: Certification Terms, Effective Dates and Recertification — Medical and Life-Support Protections
content:
Each certification registered under Medical and Life-Support Protections is valid for a term counted in months from its certified date. The term, the point at which the allowance and the protections begin and end, the recertification reminder and the grace period after expiration are set per protection.

## Term and recertification figures

| Protection | Term from the certified date (months) | Reminder sent before expiration (calendar days) | Grace period after expiration (calendar days) | New practitioner form needed for every renewal or recertification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medical Emergency Certificate | 1 | 0 (no reminder is sent) | 0 (no grace period) | yes |
| Standard Medical Baseline Allowance | 12 | 60 | 30 | yes |
| Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance | 12 | 60 | 30 | yes |
| Combined Medical Baseline Allowance | 12 | 60 | 30 | yes |
| Life-Support Registration | 24 | 60 | 45 | yes |
| Critical Care Life-Support Registration | 24 | 90 | 60 | yes |

## When the allowance and the protections begin

| Protection | Beginning |
|---|---|
| Medical Emergency Certificate | protection begins on the date the certification is registered |
| Standard Medical Baseline Allowance, Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance, Combined Medical Baseline Allowance, Life-Support Registration, Critical Care Life-Support Registration | allowance begins with the first bill whose billing period ends after the certified date; protections begin on the certified date |

## What ends when a certification expires

| Protection | Effect of expiration |
|---|---|
| Medical Emergency Certificate | postponement and protections end on the expiration date |
| Standard Medical Baseline Allowance, Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance, Combined Medical Baseline Allowance, Life-Support Registration, Critical Care Life-Support Registration | allowance stops with bills whose billing period ends after the expiration date; protections end on the expiration date |

## Points of reading

- For the Medical Emergency Certificate the start is tied to the date the certification is **registered**; for the other five protections the protections start on the **certified date** and the allowance starts with a bill.
- The allowance start and stop are both judged by the date on which a bill's billing period **ends**: the first bill whose period ends after the certified date is the first bill with the allowance, and bills whose period ends after the expiration date no longer receive it.
- A grace period of 0 means there is none; a reminder figure of 0 means no reminder is sent. Both apply to the Medical Emergency Certificate.

### Hypothetical illustration

A Standard Medical Baseline Allowance is certified on 10 May, and the agreement's billing periods end on the 20th of each month. The billing period ending 20 May ends after the certified date, so that bill is the first to carry the allowance, while the protections themselves begin on 10 May. If the certification's expiration date later falls on 9 May of a following year, the bill whose period ends 20 April still carries the allowance, and the bill whose period ends 20 May of that year does not.
